summary: Okta device_id canonicalization change breaks SSH handoff for runbook elevated sessions
description: Issue summary: After the Okta device_id canonicalization change rolled 2026-03-11, several oncall engineers report immediate failures when attempting to escalate into runbook sessions that require SSH handoff. Impact: Blocked runbook escalations for oncall leads; unable to complete emergency remediation steps via bastion. Intermittent occurrence but now reproducible for sessions issued before and after the device claim variant switch. Environment: production (us-west) identity proxy + SSH bastion. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start an elevated runbook that requires SSH handoff from the runbook portal. 2) Trigger a device-bound SSO flow (Okta device assertion present). 3) Observe the bastion attempt to validate the device_id claim during session handoff. Observed behavior: Bastion rejects the handoff with 403 and logs show failed device claim match: "device_id mismatch canonical form: expected base64urlsafe, got base64+padding". Users see "Elevated session failed to establish" and cannot access the target host. Expected behavior: Device assertion canonicalization should be normalized by identity-proxy so both legacy and new device_id encodings are accepted and handoff succeeds. Immediate impact: Two active oncall pages delayed ~20–40 minutes while engineers worked around by creating short-lived SSH keys, causing minor incident escalation.
investigation:
Initial hypotheses: Okta started sending device_id with padded base64 in some tenants after a mobile Okta client update; identity-proxy validates exact device_id string which fails binary-equivalent encodings.
Logs and traces:
- identity-proxy auth logs show 403 at 2026-03-12T09:15:22Z with tag device-claim-validate-failed.
- Bastion logs: /var/log/bastion/handshake.log lines referencing claim_value 'QmFzZTY0U2FtcGxl==' vs canonical 'QmFzZTY0U2FtcGxl' (padding difference).
- Correlated Slack thread: #support-identity thread ts 2026-03-12T09:18 (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01ABC/thread-159).
- Affected sessions count: ~7 failed handoffs in last 6 hours, historically 0.
Workarounds attempted: 1) Identity team temporarily patched a proxy rule to strip padding in a canary edge for dev-bastion (PR linked above). 2) Oncall created temporary SSH keys as a stopgap. Repro rate: 100% for device assertions that include '=' padding.
Next steps suggested: 1) Add normalization step in identity-proxy device claim validator to accept both padded and unpadded base64 variants. 2) Backfill one-hour log window to identify all impacted sessions. 3) Post-deploy run of e2e runbook handoff tests across device-assertion variants.
comments: Priya Nair (reporter) 2026-03-12: Observed first failure during an after-hours ops run; created ticket and escalated to oncall.
Maya Chen (assignee) 2026-03-12: Triaging — reproduced locally using a crafted device assertion with '=' padding. Captured failing stack trace in identity-proxy. Marking Sev1 due to runbook impact.
SRE Oncall (2026-03-12): Applied dev-edge workaround that strips padding for requests from dev-bastion; requesting a safe rollout plan for prod.
Identity Team (2026-03-13): Confirmed Okta client update rolled 2026-03-11 changed device assertion encoding for some mobile agents. Preparing PR to normalize encoding during validation.
Maya Chen (2026-03-14): PR for identity-proxy normalization submitted and linked. Requesting review from infra-security for compatibility and threat analysis.
resolution_notes: Mitigation in progress: normalization PR submitted to identity-proxy; canaryed on dev and staging. Plan to roll to prod in two phases with feature flag and trace-level logging to monitor acceptance rate. Follow-up actions: automated e2e for device-claim variants, postmortem to include Okta client change detection in release notes.
next_steps: 1) Security review of normalization change (expected safe) 2) Merge + feature-flag rollout to prod 3) Run backfill to enumerate affected sessions and notify any impacted users 4) Add unit and e2e tests for both padded and unpadded device_id encodings
